photos.source_note: Instagram is the business's own primary photo channel (@jgmconstruction.fl, verified real, see instagram_note); Facebook only yielded a profile picture. Additional real photos recovered from a Yahoo Local business listing (local.yahoo.com) which hosts 5 first-party images uploaded under this exact business's listing (phone 407-747-2700, address 3826 Bay Club Cir). Of 12 Instagram posts and 5 Yahoo Local photos (17 candidates total), most were marketing ad graphics with heavy text overlays (kitchen/bathroom/painting promo flyers with a cartoon mascot), one was an unrelated car-wash canopy photo, one was a personal ribbon-cutting/home-reveal video screenshot with a 'YES' text overlay, one was a dark/overexposed garage ceiling shot, and one was a screenshot of a Florida Sunbiz LLC filing document (not a work photo). After visual curation (reading every candidate image before choosing), only 5 photos were real, untouched by text overlays, in focus and clearly this business's own work: a finished bathroom remodel, a marble-look tile floor installation, a jobsite photo of Juan holding the company's business card next to a fresh concrete sidewalk pour, and two in-progress drywall repair close-ups (corner bead and seam). This is right at the 5-photo minimum; no further real, clean photos were found after exhausting Instagram, Facebook, Yahoo Local, Yelp (blocked by anti-bot, could not fetch), Nextdoor (generic placeholder images only, no real photos), and bizprofile.net (no photos, only tracking scripts).

palette_note: Terracotta/copper palette (accent-deep #b5651d, accent-mid #d68a4c) over a warm cream base, derived independently from the construction/remodeling niche (not from any specific brand asset since the business's own marketing uses a black/gold generic template). Chosen to be visually distinct from the plum-pink and teal-acero palettes already used elsewhere in this repo, and distinct from a blue-steel palette reportedly in use for a handyman business in the same city (Kissimmee), per task instructions.

The only hours-like data point (a Birdeye/business-directory listing showing 'Monday-Saturday 12:00 a.m. to Midnight, Sunday 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.') reads as a generic 24/7 directory default rather than credible posted hours for a contractor, so hours were omitted from the site entirely rather than shown as unreliable data.
